speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me if the double vision or weakness has been getting progressively worse over the past few weeks or months? Also, do you experience any difficulty swallowing or changes in your speech?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does your double vision or eyelid drooping fluctuate throughout the day, often worsening by evening? I would also like to know if you have any history of thyroid disease or recent infections.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any difficulty swallowing or changes in your speech, such as a nasal voice? I would also like to know if you have had any recent weight loss or palpitations.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibody_Test. REQUEST TEST: Electromyography.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated); Electromyography: Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation

speaker: Doctor
text: The test results confirm the diagnosis of Myasthenia Gravis, characterized by elevated acetylcholine receptor antibodies and decreased muscle response on repetitive stimulation. DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
